themes.consensus_view: The desks agree hyperscaler spending on AI data centers keeps getting revised higher and demand still exceeds available capacity, but they split on whether that spending is a durable investment cycle or an overbuild increasingly paid for with borrowed money.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscaler capital spending plans for 2026 keep being revised upward and AI demand is still running ahead of available compute capacity.
evidence_quotes: AI demand continues to outstrip available capacity, with cloud backlogs at record levels
aggregate 2026 spend now tracking to ~$750b (+80% y/y)
continued upward revisions to hyperscaler capex and WFE as constructive for the European semicap complex

facts_agreed.claim: The latest round of big-cloud earnings was read as confirmation that the AI spending trade is still working.
evidence_quotes: the Big 3 all reported very solid results that appear to confirm that the AI trade is alive and well
current stock performance underestimates META’s ability to scale and productize and/or monetize compute

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscaler capex, how it is funded, and whether it earns a return are being tracked as a live subject across every major desk in this window.

facts_contested.claim: Whether the debt-funded portion of the AI buildout is a real risk to the spending cycle
facts_contested.for_evidence: Hyperscaler credit concerns seem to be overstated
facts_contested.against_evidence: most TS Lombard clients share our doubts about the sustainability of the AI bubble

themes.consensus_view: Six desks keep referencing the Strait of Hormuz as a live oil-shipping risk and an active negotiation story, but none of them has staked out a directional call on where it goes.

facts_agreed.claim: Six banks flag the Strait of Hormuz as a live energy-shipping risk this window, treating it as the chokepoint where oil supply could get squeezed.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy supply disruption

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks also track the diplomatic track around the Strait as a separate live thread, framing negotiations and a return to normal shipping as the other side of the story.

themes.theme: warsh fed chairmanship and press conferences
themes.consensus_view: Six desks are watching Kevin Warsh's run as Fed chair and his post-meeting press conferences as a live driver of rate expectations, but none has staked out a directional call on what he does next.

facts_agreed.claim: Six research desks flag Kevin Warsh's Fed chairmanship and his credibility as a live macro topic this window.
Multiple desks single out the Warsh FOMC press conference itself as the event to watch, with one reading it as leaning toward easier policy.

themes.consensus_view: The Fed has stopped spelling out how it decides policy, and most desks read that as a credibility problem that adds uncertainty and bigger market swings, even as one house still holds a firm call that rates go higher this year.

facts_agreed.claim: Pulling back forward guidance without explaining how the Fed decides policy raises uncertainty and erodes the Fed's credibility.
evidence_quotes: If you remove forward guidance while simultaneously obscuring the methodology, credibility can deteriorate
You can provide less information on the reaction function but that just means more uncertainty

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks flag the Fed's missing guidance and unclear decision framework as an active market issue this window.
evidence_quotes: Lack of forward guidance from Fed Chair

facts_agreed.claim: The July FOMC produced three dissents in favor of a rate hike.

facts_contested.claim: whether the Fed's next policy move is readable enough to forecast
facts_contested.for_evidence: Our baseline remains that the Fed raises rates by 50bps this year
facts_contested.against_evidence: If you remove forward guidance while simultaneously obscuring the methodology, credibility can deteriorate

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the extra yield investors demand for holding long-dated government bonds is rebuilding as the Fed stops telling markets where rates go next, and the unresolved question is whether that long-end breakout forces stocks to reprice.

facts_agreed.claim: The extra yield investors demand for owning long-dated bonds is rising again, and desks are positioned for it to keep rising rather than fade.
evidence_quotes: The Fed’s move away from forward guidance is adding more term premium back to bond yields.
We continue to hold higher term premium positions in both US and European rates

facts_agreed.claim: Bond market volatility has come back as a live cross-desk risk, with the long end of the curve the focal point.
Long-end US yields are breaking out of a multi-year range while market-implied inflation is moving the way it did in 2022.
evidence_quotes: Years of consolidation in the US 10-year are now being tested.
10Y breakevens enduring a move that looked more akin to 2022

themes.consensus_view: The crowded momentum trade (money piled into the stocks that had been rising fastest, mostly AI and chip names) has broken hard and every desk is tracking the damage, but banks split on whether the selling is now exhausted or the bounce is just forced short covering running into resistance.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks confirm the momentum factor has gone through a sharp, measurable unwind rather than a normal rotation.
evidence_quotes: Retail investors have been quick to cut Tech exposure as the Semis-led Momentum Unwind

facts_agreed.claim: The unwind is driven by crowded, identical positioning, so the reversal forces investors to cut exposure rather than reflecting a change in fundamentals.
evidence_quotes: when you’re positioned the same way as everyone else, and the trend changes
rebound in tech and momentum stocks looks more like a positioning squeeze
Retail investors have been quick to cut Tech exposure as the Semis-led Momentum Unwind

facts_agreed.claim: Momentum is now treated as a broad read on the AI trade and hedge fund exposure, not a niche quant strategy, and desks are tracking that exposure directly.
evidence_quotes: Momentum has become much more than an obscure quant strategy.
US High Beta Momentum versus SPX realized vol spread

facts_contested.claim: whether the momentum unwind is exhausted and a durable rebound follows
facts_contested.against_evidence: expect a choppier, range bound tape for momentum rather than an explosive rebound

facts_contested.claim: what the tech and momentum rebound actually is: start of risk-on versus a positioning squeeze into resistance
facts_contested.against_evidence: rebound in tech and momentum stocks looks more like a positioning squeeze

themes.consensus_view: Four desks agree Japan's currency is now being propped up by official yen-buying and a central bank that keeps lifting rates, which forces an exit from the popular trade of borrowing cheap yen to buy higher-yielding assets elsewhere, and none of them argue for a return to a weak yen.

facts_agreed.claim: Official yen-buying intervention, coordinated between US and Japanese authorities, is the live driver every desk is tracking on this theme.
evidence_quotes: Last week's intervention and rate checks have already jolted what had been an unusually steady uptrend

facts_agreed.claim: The policy and valuation backdrop points to a stronger yen: the Bank of Japan is still raising its policy rate while the currency is viewed as unusually cheap.
evidence_quotes: the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate
it felt like one of the most obvious medium-term trades in markets and still does

themes.consensus_view: Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan both keep Middle East conflict on the risk list as a background threat, but neither desk has taken a side on whether it gets worse or how markets would move if it does.

facts_agreed.claim: Two banks flag Middle East conflict as a live risk in this window without staking a directional view on it.
